turn_text: So he has put his finger on the identity crisis that the Republican Party is going through. I think I think the Republican Party has to learn from this Trump era. And there are many lessons. But some lessons are actually not just negative, right? I think there's some positive lessons here, too. I think Donald Trump taught Republicans that a political party has to appeal to a broader base of people. So the Republican Party for many years, certainly the party that I grew up in, talked a lot about economic policy and how certain policies are good for corporations and job creators. Certainly, I legislated along those lines when we cut corporate taxes. Why? And then we thought that still think that was a great decision. American companies were paying a 35% tax rate. That made them a lot less competitive than companies in most countries throughout the world were paying in the 20s. So we thought it was a good idea, and I still strongly believe it was a good idea to cut the corporate tax rate so that US companies can do better, employ more people, invest more, et cetera. But those are economic arguments. Those are intellectual arguments. A political party also has to be popular. in order to win. And I think for many years, Republican messaging had become stale and a lot of Americans had lost their ability to relate to Republican message. Again, Donald Trump really changed that. Now he did it in a way I strongly disagree with because He sowed a lot of resentment and anger in society and made people feel insecure and ultimately provoked them to be violent. But there's still a lesson there. Perhaps the Republican Party doesn't have to become totally populist, even though it is trending in that direction, but certainly it must do a better job of connecting the dots for people and helping people understand why free market capitalism is the best policy for them and for their families. Even if it means that sometimes people fail and businesses close and people apply for jobs and lose to more qualified candidates. That's competition. That's the nature of it. But even if we might lose today, In the long run, we all win because we're more productive as a society, people have more choice. So we do need to learn from Donald Trump, this lesson that political parties, political movements, political platforms. not only need to make policy sense, but they have to be popular and they have to appeal to people beyond those who sit in corporate boardrooms. So free trade is another important example of that. I think the reason or one of the reasons why a lot of Americans turned against free trade policies is because We didn't do a good enough job of explaining how that all works and of highlighting the many jobs and opportunities that free and fair trade do generate here in our country. So I do think that Trump has left an indelible mark in the party. In this sense, I do think that the party will have a populist streak, which it really didn't 10 years ago.
